speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This was a significant milestone in our global fight against climate change and for all who seek a sustainable future for our children.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: When we strip away its legalities, the heart of this pact is really about energy use and conservation.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The International Energy Agency's World Energy Outlook 2016 projected in its "main scenario" that global energy demand would rise by 30% from now to 2040, with accompanying increases in greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Reducing energy use is thus key to address global warming.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Faced with an increasingly carbon-constrained future, countries and businesses have no choice but to transform the way we produce and use energy.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: At the same time, this has given rise to new opportunities to grow a greener and more sustainable economy.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For example, China is embracing renewables in a big way, while India plans to have nearly 60% of its electricity capacity come from non-fossil fuels by 2027.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Google has committed to power 100% of its operations with renewables.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I visited Shell's "Make the Future" exhibition last month which showcased innovative ideas to harness energy without emitting more carbon.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One such example was a wind turbine that could capture wind energy produced by cars travelling along a highway.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: While innovative technologies can supplement our energy needs, Singapore will still have to depend on imported energy, primarily natural gas, which is cleaner than oil and coal, to meet the bulk of our demand.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our energy demand is projected to increase at a compounded annual growth rate of between 1.2% and 1.8% over the next decade.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Given our limited land space, we are disadvantaged in our ability to use alternative energy.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Improving energy efficiency (EE) in the industrial sector is thus key to achieving our climate change goals.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In 2012, we introduced the Energy Conservation Act (ECA).

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our main objective was to put in place the building blocks to help the industry develop its capabilities in EE.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under ECA, 180 energy-intensive companies, accounting for the lion's share of industrial energy use, are required to implement basic energy management practices, such as regular monitoring of energy use and to appoint qualified energy managers, to oversee EE improvements.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ECA companies have reported an overall EE improvement rate of 0.4% and 0.6% in 2014 and 2015 respectively.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It is timely to bring our efforts to the next level.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The EC Bill that my Ministry is proposing aims to introduce three sets of enhancements to the original ECA.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The first, and where the bulk of enhancements are, is on measures to improve our industrial EE.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The second set seeks to improve greenhouse gas emissions reporting, and the third deals with the new Vehicular Emissions Scheme (VES).

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will introduce three enhancements to strengthen EE practices among ECA companies.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: They are: one, the adoption of structured Energy Management Systems (EnMSs); two, to conduct regular EE opportunities assessments; and three, to conduct design reviews.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our analysis of ECA data in 2014 and 2015 showed several areas for improvement.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In particular, we found that many companies did not adopt a structured framework to manage their energy use and guide their EE efforts.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In addition, EE ambition amongst companies continued to be low.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The proposed amendments to the EC Bill will thus require ECA companies to adopt a structured EnMS.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: EnMS institutes a "plan, do, check, act" framework for companies to constantly re-examine and improve their EE efforts.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Senior management will be responsible for setting energy policy and targets, evaluating them and developing action plans.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Studies have shown that having a structured EnMS can help companies achieve energy savings of at least 10% to 15% in the first few years.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Countries like Japan and those in the EU have already incorporated this practice in their regulations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With this amendment, companies will be required to put in place an EnMS by 2021 or 2022, depending on the size of their facility's energy consumption.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: ECA companies will also be required to conduct regular Energy Efficiency Opportunities Assessments (EEOAs).

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Also known as energy audits, EEOAs involve systematic assessments of energy consumption and the identification and quantification of potential improvement opportunities.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Large companies in the EU, South Korea and India are already required to conduct such assessments regularly.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under the enhanced ECA, companies will be required to submit their first EEOA by 2021.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many companies have given feedback that the lifespan of industrial equipment can be very long of 30 years or more.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thus, it is challenging to introduce new technologies midway as it disrupts their operations.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Instead, it is better to identify and incorporate EE opportunities at the start of the project.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The three key enhancements that I have just detailed are intended to help ingrain good EE practices among companies.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Thus far, ECA data also showed that many companies have focused on harvesting "low-hanging fruits", or EE measures that have short pay-back periods that provide only low energy savings.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Undertaking EE improvements for larger systems, such as boilers, chillers and compressed air systems, would significantly enhance the savings reaped.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The data also showed much room for improvement in the EE of common industrial equipment like motors.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Hence, the Bill will aim to increase the adoption of more energy-efficient commonly­ used industrial equipment and systems.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: An existing measure under ECA is the Minimum Energy Performance Standards (MEPS).

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: However, I would like to point out that the overall benefits of the ECA measures to companies are by far more attractive, including helping them to achieve long-term cost savings and increased competitiveness.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The second set of enhancements that will be made to ECA concerns the reporting of greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These enhancements aim to strengthen the Quality Assurance and Quality Control processes within our Measurement and Reporting (M&R) requirements, to provide a robust foundation for the future carbon pricing regime.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Large industrial emitters will be required to submit a monitoring plan and an enhanced greenhouse gas emissions report based on the approved monitoring plan.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Companies will also have to compute their emissions data according to standard methodologies determined by the National Environment Agency (NEA).

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These will bring our M&R standards in line with international best practices and ensure accurate and robust accounting of their emissions.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will also help companies to better understand and manage their emissions.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The third set of revisions to ECA concerns the VES.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Under CEVS, only carbon dioxide is taken into consideration in determining the emissions level in a vehicle.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: VES, which replaces it, will now consider other harmful pollutant emissions in addition to carbon dioxide.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Any label on any motor vehicle model displayed for sale-end related promotional materials and advertisements must now include information of the vehicular emissions of the motor vehicle, including information on the fuel economy of the motor vehicle.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The EC Bill proposes to amend the ECA to extend the labelling and information disclosure requirements related to VES and to make the relevant amendments to the Road Traffic Act to give effect to the new scheme.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The proposed enhancements to the ECA are forward-looking and aim to guide how we view and conserve precious energy resources.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The ECA provides a framework to shape positive choices in the industry, transport and household sectors to achieve a carbon-efficient and sustainable future.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: It will also catalyse demand for EE and clean energy services, which could become the seeds of future growth.

speaker: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: I encourage all stakeholders to work with us on efforts to conserve energy, as we seek a sustainable future together.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Our industrial sector is the largest consumer of energy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: From now until then, we will require a consistent improvement rate of 1% to 2% each year.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We certainly have work cut out for us and we absolutely must take a tougher stance on EE.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Certainly, to improve the current situation, it is vital that we must have a clear understanding of what is expected.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This means accurately monitoring energy usage, and then using the results, analyse how and how much one can reduce, if necessary.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In South Korea and the EU, companies are required to conduct regular energy audits, usually every three to five years.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In place of conducting energy assessments, large companies in the EU can also choose to adopt internationally-certified EnMS, such as ISO 5001.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The proposed enhancements to the ECA are thus a move in the right direction.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is wise to mandate that large industrial facilities are to submit a monitoring plan and, subsequently, an improved emissions report to NEA.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: By making it compulsory for these facilities to adopt methodologies that are in line with internationally recognised protocols, this brings us yet another step further towards international standards for climate-friendly nations.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In the meantime, energy-intensive companies in Singapore have been reporting their energy usage since the introduction of the ECA in 2013.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister share some insights from these reports, and how the ECA amendments will help to raise the bar for energy-efficient standards of common industrial equipment?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I would also propose more encouragement and incentives for companies to adopt EnMS and software approved by NEA.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Rather than adopt a sit­-and-wait approach, reacting to the results from monitoring energy usage, it would be more efficient and productive to get companies started on a good energy management plan.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: As the need for these EnMSs becomes more prominent, I foresee great potential in this industry and I hope the relevant Government agencies will do more to promote the quality and capability of local EnMSs.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Last year, global energy service provider ENGlE officially opened its first laboratory in Asia in Singapore with support from the Economic Development Board.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This laboratory is part of an international research and development (R&D) network, supported by 1,100 researchers and experts worldwide.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It focuses on smart energy systems for cities and islands, industrial EE and gas technologies.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Are there plans to collaborate with and tap on this network?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This will first apply to motors, gradually extending to include other systems and equipment.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I am pleased to note that this new standard is being implemented gradually.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: While I think it is a good policy to have, it requires a significant amount of change on top of other existing restructuring efforts.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Certainly, in the long run, businesses will gain through savings from improved EE.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But in the short term, in trying to kickstart the new systems and auditing processes, this could be a burden for companies, especially in the current economic climate.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I have spoken with some business owners, who expressed their concerns about the startup costs of implementing and maintaining the new systems.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Moreover, how does the Ministry intend to support them?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I think this is important, especially in the initial years, to get companies on the right track.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The first and early steps are always the hardest.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First of all, I commend this move, as earlier on, the various overlapping schemes and incentives had made it confusing and time-consuming for businesses to tap on them.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Hopefully, with this new Fund in place, the take-up rate will become considerably higher.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: My next concern is how accessible the funds are, whether the release of funds will be done at the start of the project or after it is completed, with justification of evidence of expenses.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is applicable to households, and that is because residential buildings are responsible for the majority of energy consumed in the city.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: The Brussels Green Loan is available to Brussels households with a limited income and it will eventually be extended to all households.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope the Government will consider something similar for businesses, as sometimes it is challenging for businesses to kickstart something without sufficient capital.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Energy storage should be another major component in a comprehensive far-sighted strategy for energy sufficiency.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Considering our small geographical size, energy storage would be vital in supporting greater deployment of photovoltaic systems or solar power systems.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It could potentially be a game changer for our electricity market in the near future.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: It is clear that there is a globally shared understanding on the importance of energy management in combating climate change.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: So, energy services in facilities management will certainly continue to be in demand in the years to come.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: To make the entire framework sustainable, there needs to be continuity and this means a long-sighted approach, nurturing talents of tomorrow.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: We must not only focus on energy management within industries but also on the provision of these energy services management.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: In recent years, several courses have been developed by the local universities and polytechnics, offering degrees and diplomas in energy management and the like.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: What is the take-up rate of these courses, and how many students eventually graduate to work in a related field of their studies?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Singapore's efforts to maximise EE may be intrusive for businesses but should be embraced for the potential positive impact it would have, not just on the environment but on the economy.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: But in any country, this will require a multiple-pronged approach that involves the government, businesses and individuals.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: (In Mandarin):   This amendment will require many companies to improve their EE.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: This is for the sake of the earth.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: However, the current economic situation is not looking good, many small and medium enterprises (SMEs) are worried about the cost.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I hope that the Government can pay attention and help them.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: I also hope that the Government can pay attention to EE in households.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Can we do what Belgium has done and help households improve their EE?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: With countries promising to reduce their emission under the Paris Agreement, the world economy could see business opportunities worth $19 trillion in areas, such as energy management.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Does Singapore have sufficient talents in this area?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: And how is the Government going to help our enterprises to seize these business opportunities?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Meeting these obligations is a matter of being responsible global citizens.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: But this is also about serving the national interest of Singapore, since we have the interest in managing sea level, ensuring clean air for our citizens and so on and so forth.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I do not object to the thrust of the Bill, but I do have some queries and suggestions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I agree that this is generally a good move, as it means that adopting a broader and more relevant definition of pollutant emissions, now in encompassing hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide, nitrogen oxide and particulate matter.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Rather, the rebates and surcharges are based on the vehicles' capacity to emit carbon or pollutants.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can this be considered post-2020, with the introduction of the ERP2.0 system?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If this is introduced, it should be revenue-neutral with additional surcharges for mileage offset against other cost borne by motorists.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I would like to query the provisions relating to conducting an EEOA, so as to obtain a clearance certificate for a new venture, which is contained in a newly inserted section 26A.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Existing businesses are also required to conduct such assessments for prescribed activities and premises under the new section 27(B).

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In the new section 27(B), an is defined as a systematic procedure by which adequate knowledge of energy consumption profile of any business activities or premises and cost-effective EE opportunities are identified and quantified.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Ministry should also provide more guidance to those producing such assessments, whether they are done in-house or by third parties, to ensure that these assessments can be done in a focused and, hence, cost-effective way that meets the requirements of the law.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Minimising the risk of over-reporting, and hence of consultancies over-charging, or of internal resources being wasted.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: This is not the first in our series of bold commitments towards environmental protection, following on from the recent announcement of the carbon tax and, last year, in requiring sustainability reporting from all listed companies.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Since the ECA was brought into effect in 2013, it appears that companies have been able to fulfil the Act's requirements to implement certain basic energy management practices.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: These include appointing at least one certified energy manager and reporting their energy use and greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Thus, it seems like a natural next step to enhance the Act by requiring industrial facilities to submit a monitoring plan and emissions report in line with international standards.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: He mentioned that operational and capability constraints and inefficient common industrial equipment could be the reason for lower EE rates in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I believe that another reason could also be the highly specialised and integrated nature of Singapore's industrial sector, which leaves little room for downtime.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Improving EE often requires equipment upgrades, but such upgrades are likely to cause disruptions to operations and come at a cost.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Furthermore, companies operating on thin margins may avoid proposing improvements to EE, as this often involves high capital costs and adds pressure to their bottom line.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Management often approves projects that meet the dual criteria of low investment cost and short pay-back periods, and projects on EE may not meet this mark.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Can the Minister provide more details about this and on when we can expect to receive updates on these revised incentive schemes?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: As an indication of how receptive the industry is towards Government support for EE, can the Minister share information on the take-up rate of the key schemes that I have listed?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Was there a slow take-up rate and could slow take-up rates have contributed to low EE improvement rates?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I also note that EE grants are being consolidated under the Energy Efficiency Fund (E2F).

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Does the Ministry of the Environment and Water Resources (MEWR) believe that consolidation will lead to better take-up rates?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: What measures can be taken to improve the take-up rate of E2F as well?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: I raise these points to ask for further clarity on how we are providing that support, beyond strengthened requirements for monitoring and reporting, as proposed by this Bill.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: That said, I applaud this Bill for announcing bold steps in ensuring that Singapore meets its Conference of the Parties (COP21) commitments and I stand in support of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Globally, we see a shift towards a carbon-constrained economy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This momentum is partly driven by countries working towards meeting their commitments under the Paris Agreement.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: But there is also an increasing realisation that we all, as individuals and corporations alike, cannot continue with business as usual.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The impacts can be devastating as some countries and cities are already feeling this impact.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: So, even as we strengthen our resilience to deal with the unexpected, we all have a responsibility to take action now to reduce our carbon footprint.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The challenge then is whether we are prepared to make decisive moves, to take difficult decisions today and seize new opportunities as they arise, so that our nation can continue to grow and prosper in a very carbon-constrained world.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Status quo is, therefore, not an option, if we are not to be left behind.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Global companies, such as Apple and Unilever, have also set ambitious goals to "green" their practices.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These are just a few of the many developments around the world.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We must not delude ourselves into thinking that we can stay where we are.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To maintain Singapore's international competitiveness in the long run, we need to ready ourselves for a carbon-light future.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah asked what will happen if we do not meet our Paris Agreement commitments.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Singapore has a strong international reputation to uphold and, as a responsible global citizen, we are committed to fulfilling the pledge.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To achieve this, we will have to implement tough mitigation measures in all key sectors, not just in the industrial sector, but also in the transport, building, power and household sectors.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee also asked for insights from the Energy Use Reports reported under ECA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In addition to companies having low ambition, we found that the majority of companies − 60% − did not have EE improvement plans beyond the first two years.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A significant proportion of the common utility systems, such as boilers, chillers and compressed air systems, were operating inefficiently.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, the enhancements in this Bill aim to help companies improve their energy practices and raise the bar for EE performance standards in Singapore, starting with motors.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To illustrate, motors collectively account for 80% of the total electricity consumed by the industry.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Unfortunately, Singapore is an alternative energy disadvantaged country because of our physical size.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Solar energy remains our best option, but even this is not without its challenges.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We have been exploring innovative ways to overcome our constraints.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: For example, in 2016, Singapore embarked on the world's largest floating solar testbed at Tengeh Reservoir.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: All these initiatives open up new business opportunities for our companies.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To keep pace with the growing share of solar energy in Singapore's electricity generation mix, we are also taking proactive steps to address the issue of intermittency and to ensure grid stability.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In May 2016, the Energy Market Authority (EMA) and Singapore Power embarked on the national Energy Storage System testbed (ESS testbed), to evaluate the performance of grid-level energy storage systems for different power applications.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee asked for an update of the project.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: There was strong interest from consortiums comprising notable local and international companies when the Request for Proposal (RFP) closed in August 2016.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: An international evaluation panel, comprising Singapore Power, relevant Government agencies and technical experts, is currently reviewing the various proposals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: A decision on the eventual award winners will likely be made by end 2017.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Given the challenges we face with renewable energy today, improving our EE thus remains a key strategy for Singapore.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Companies understand the need for EE improvement and are generally agreeable with our proposals.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: I am heartened by their commitment to keep working at improving EE.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Er Dr Lee and Mr Leon Perera raised the issue of compliance costs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In the short term, companies under ECA will face an increase in compliance costs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: However, in the long run, these enhanced EE measures will help companies reap lifetime energy and cost savings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Many of these big companies already have inhouse systems and standards and the reporting systems that we can rely on, and we will use this first.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hopefully, this can be used for our verification purposes and not impose standards that will be too onerous.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Hence, companies need to adopt a long-term view as these measures will put them on a stronger footing to compete in the carbon-constrained world that we will be operating in.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: In my dialogues with the companies, some of them sought funding support to implement related EE-measures and asked whether the Government can help to improve the supporting EE ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Under E2F, companies no longer have to navigate through different incentive schemes to find one that suits their needs.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The grant application process has also been streamlined to minimise paperwork.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: E2F will be launched today and I encourage companies to tap on it.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Mr Louis Ng also asked for details of the EE Financing Programme and Investment Allowance Scheme for EE administered by the Economic Development Board (EDB).

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The EE Financing Programme is in the pilot stage.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Essentially, companies which are not able to afford the upfront costs of EE projects can apply for loans through a third-party financier.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: The potential benefits of such a scheme include an off balance sheet solution, where industrial facilities are not required to pay for the upfront costs of the EE projects, but still enjoy part of the energy savings.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: These two schemes provide alternative financing options for companies which want to pursue EE efforts but need more financial support.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As the EE Financing Programme is still in the pilot stage, more updates will be provided in due course.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Aside from financial support, we will study how we can improve the supporting EE ecosystem.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: This includes enabling more sharing of best practices amongst companies, building up the capabilities of energy managers to identify EE opportunities, and developing the energy services sub-sector, such as consultancies for specialised industry processes.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: We will also continue to leverage research and technology to improve EE and are open to working with interested partners and stakeholders.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Lastly, developing talent in this sector is important, too.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: As Er Dr Lee highlighted, local polytechnics and the Building and Construction Authority (BCA) offer diploma programmes related to energy management.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: NEA and the Institution of Engineers also administer the Singapore Certified Energy Manager Professional Level programme.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Individuals who wish to pursue a career in energy management, including those making mid-career switches, can apply for this programme.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Many of them take on energy management roles in about 230 energy-intensive industrial facilities that are regulated under ECA.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: To conclude, the amendments to this Bill are an important step forward not only in encouraging industry and consumers to play their part in addressing climate change, but also in preparing us for a carbon-constrained global economy.

speaker: Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M
text: Therefore, I call on Members of the House to give their support to this Bill.
